### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 95e24b0096636e55b409fb217da3fa44832104c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9f0f2a891fc5132eb12b4d637bee8192d9ebed9c` — the merge of head `3a0bcb2d1403d7da537230fa309a7762d1abde0c` into base `95e24b0096636e55b409fb217da3fa44832104c1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9f0f2a891fc5132eb12b4d637bee8192d9ebed9c && git checkout 9f0f2a891fc5132eb12b4d637bee8192d9ebed9c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 95e24b0096636e55b409fb217da3fa44832104c1 3a0bcb2d1403d7da537230fa309a7762d1abde0c && git checkout -B drift-repro 95e24b0096636e55b409fb217da3fa44832104c1 && git merge --no-ff 3a0bcb2d1403d7da537230fa309a7762d1abde0c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 95e24b0096636e55b409fb217da3fa44832104c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3a0bcb2d1403d7da537230fa309a7762d1abde0c`
Local-runs: none

Isolated contract review of PR #21234 (card #21189), read-only. Inputs: the card body and every comment on it (triage 5935183237, claim 5938468669, dev report 5939634586), the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` (3 files, +79 / -12), the code on `origin/main` (`95e24b00`) that the published text describes, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the dev's SQLite measurements were not repeated, the code was read instead.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set and public surface: nothing moves — right.** The diff edits one string literal (the `acceptanceCriteria` of the semantic entry `filter-text-operator-declared-type-refused`, protocol 18), its generated mirror in `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` (`step18`, byte-identical to the entry), and adds one changeset. No Zod schema, export, type, enum, operator set, error code, conversion or refusal changes; the entry's `id`, `surface`, `replacement` and `reason` are untouched. The text IS published (`@objectstack/spec` maps `./migrations` to `dist/migrations`) and `objectstack migrate meta` prints it as the `verify:` line (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts`), so every sentence was judged against the code on `origin/main`. That code is identical on the PR head and on `origin/main`: the one `sql-driver.ts` change `main` gained after the merge base is the upsert refusal of #21225, and it touches none of the symbols named below.

Sentence by sentence, against `origin/main`:

1. "This door judges a field by its declared type alone, so it never refuses a text operator over a text-valued field — `select` / `radio` codes, `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags`, lookup and `user` ids, `autonumber` and the file classes." **TRUE.** `textOperatorDoorVerdict` (`packages/spec/src/data/filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts`) reads `type` only (`returnType` for `formula`); `TEXT_OPERATOR_DOOR_PASSING_TYPES` is `STRING_VALUE_TYPES` ∪ `autonumber` ∪ `SINGLE_OPTION_TYPES` ∪ `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` ∪ `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` ∪ `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES`, and the module states "`multiple: true` does not change a verdict". The engine door (`packages/objectql/src/text-operator-declared-type-door.ts`) consults that verdict and nothing else.
2. "Over every such field that is not stored as a JSON column, filters must keep answering exactly as before; that is the control." **TRUE.** The JSON-column gate fires only where `SqlDriver.isJsonColumn` (driver-sql), `isJsonStoredField` (driver-memory) or `declaredJsonStoredFields` (objectql, per-aggregation `filter`) answer true; no other column's text-operator answer moved in #21009.
3. "A field stored as a JSON column is NOT that control, because a separate door judges it by its storage rather than its declared type." **TRUE**, one note: on the engine and memory faces the JSON-stored population is itself derived from the declaration (`STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES.has(type) || isMultiValueField(def)`); only driver-sql additionally reads a deployment state (`fileColumnsMoved`). The distinction the sentence draws — a type-class door against a JSON-column door — is the one the code draws, and the shared module's own header calls its subject "a field stored as a JSON column".
4. The population. "`multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags`, any field declared `multiple: true` (a multi-valued lookup or `user` among them)" **TRUE**: `isMultiValueField` is `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` ∪ (`MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` — `select`, `radio`, `lookup`, `user`, `file`, `image` — with `multiple: true`), and `FieldSchema` refuses `multiple: true` on every other type (entry `field-multiple-non-capable-type-refused`), so "any field declared `multiple: true`" is exact. "and, on a SQL deployment still inside the ADR-0104 dual-encoding window (its media columns not yet moved), a single-value file-class field" **TRUE**: `SqlDriver.isJsonField` answers `mediaColumnIsJson()` for a non-multi `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES` member, and `mediaColumnIsJson()` is `!this.fileColumnsMoved`, whose docblock reads "the one place the ADR-0104 dual-encoding window is asked about"; driver-memory (`isJsonStoredField`, which stores "the bare id, the moved end-state") and objectql (`declaredJsonStoredFields`) exclude the single-value media field by design, so the "on a SQL deployment" qualifier is right. ADR-0104's 2026-09-05 addendum is the ruling that moves that column.
5. The operator set. "every text operator there except the membership pair `$contains` / `$notContains` — `$startsWith`, `$endsWith`, `$icontains`, `$like` and `$ilike`, beside the scalar comparisons it already refused" **TRUE**: `JSON_COLUMN_INCOMPATIBLE_OPERATORS` (`packages/core/src/utils/json-column-operator-refusal.ts`) holds exactly those five text operators beside the equality, ordering, `$in` / `$nin` and `$between` family with their bare infix spellings; `$contains`, `$notContains`, `$exists`, `$null` and `$empty` are absent. `TEXT_FILTER_OPERATORS` is the seven-member list, so "every text operator except the pair" names those five and no other.
6. Code and status. "an `INVALID_FILTER` 400 that names no declared type" **TRUE** on every face that reads the set: driver-sql `jsonColumnOperatorError` → `withheldFilterError` → `unsupportedFilterError` (`code = INVALID_FILTER`, `status = 400`); driver-memory `jsonStoredFieldOperatorError` → `unsupportedFilterError`; objectql `invalidFilterError`; driver-turso's remote transport reads the same set and text. `jsonColumnOperatorRefusalText` speaks of "a multi-value or JSON field", names the field and operator in the diagnostic only, and names no declared type anywhere.
7. "so a stored filter left on one of those operators there answers that 400 after the upgrade and is outside this entry's repair list" **TRUE**: the entry defines its repair list as the messages naming "the filter key, the field's declared type and the operator"; the JSON-column message withholds field and operator and names no type, so no filter it refuses lands on that list.
8. The repair on a multi-valued field. "`$contains` for one member, an `$or` of `$contains` for any-of", "which no rewrite chooses either" **TRUE**: `containsRemedy` prescribes exactly that shape; `$contains` on a JSON column is compiled as per-dialect membership in driver-sql and as `$elemMatch` membership in driver-memory; `$or` is a combinator on every face; no ADR-0087 conversion rewrites a stored filter body, and the card records #21009's narrowing as `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
9. The single-value media repair. "it answers text operators again once its deployment finishes the media-column move (the column step of `objectstack migrate files-to-references --apply`)" **TRUE**: the command exists with an `--apply` flag (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/files-to-references.ts`, `runColumnStep`), the column step is `packages/cli/src/utils/file-column-move.ts` ("the ADR-0104 file-family COLUMN step, as a further step of `os migrate files-to-references --apply`"), it stamps `sys_migration.columns_moved_at`, which the engine's `haveFileColumnsMoved()` hands the driver at `initObjects`; `mediaColumnIsJson()` then answers false, `isJsonField` false, and the gate is never reached. `objectstack` and `os` are both declared bins of the CLI. A note for the author, not a defect in the text: the arm is frozen at `initObjects`, so a running process sees the move at its next boot; "once its deployment finishes the move" claims no live flip.
10. The changeset body repeats the same claims and adds three: "as it already refused the scalar comparisons there" (**TRUE**, since #7398), "`objectstack migrate meta` prints the corrected `verify:` line" (**TRUE**, `meta.ts`), "the generated migration registry carries the same text" (**TRUE**, the diff).

Derived gates: no path is a `GOVERNED_SURFACES` row (Governed Surface Queue Guard: success); the head repo is the base repo, so this is a delivery, not a fork proposal; the old control sentence has no carrier on `main` other than the entry and `registry.ts` (verified by `git grep`), so no pin, doc or generated artifact is left stale.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/21189-text-operator-entry-control.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, and a body carrying none of the four breaking detectors (`major`, a `**BREAKING` marker, a `!` summary, a `narrowing` arm), so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. **Right**: a correction to published text in a released package is a fix and takes `patch` — never `skip-changeset` (Post-Task Checklist step 3). The PR body's `Clause-②: no` matches the changeset's. **Clause-②: no — right**: no accept set widens or narrows; neither door's code moves; the text now describes the accept set the code already enforces.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared — nothing to answer.

The five dev deviations, each answered:

1. Population named wider than the triage parenthetical — **right**. The code holds every `multiple: true` field and the single-value media arm; triage's scope note was marked "⛔ not a ruling"; omitting them would have kept the same untrue control sentence for `select` / `radio` / `file` / `image` declared `multiple: true` and for single-value media inside the window.
2. Zero label writes — **right**. `needs:contract-review` is the dispatch seat's to hang and the record writer's to lift (contract-review reference); nothing was owed by the dev.
3. Commit trailers — **right**. AGENTS.md (Multi-agent discipline) requires the model-free trailer pair (the session-URL trailer plus `Co-authored-by: Claude`); commits `a9ee8f8f` and `e0be516a` carry exactly that pair; the merge commit `3a0bcb2d` carries none, as a merge commit does; the harness-named trailer would have been refused by the pre-push hook.
4. No test pins the sentence — **right**, verified by `git grep` on `origin/main`: the old sentence lives only in the entry and `registry.ts`; `packages/cli/test/migrate-meta-engine-guidance.test.ts` lists the entry id and checks the printed block for tracker ids only.
5. Only `registry.ts` carries the entry text — **right** (same grep; `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide do not quote `acceptanceCriteria`).

The out-of-scope finding (on a SQL deployment whose media columns have not moved, `$contains` with a single-value `file` field's exact id answers zero rows, while the JSON-column refusal on that same field prescribes `$contains`) — **ESCALATED, not a FAIL reason**. The PR's text is right and deliberately routes that field to the column move, not to `$contains`. But the dev's "reach NOT MEASURED at a public door" undersells it: the engine's declared-type door passes `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES`, so a `$startsWith` over a single-value `file` field reaches driver-sql's `assertOperatorAppliesToColumn` through `engine.find` on any such deployment — the same chain this card's premise rests on — and the 400 it answers prescribes a membership operator that has no member to find on a JSON scalar string. That is a prescription defect of `jsonColumnOperatorRefusalText` for one member of its population (or a population question in driver-sql, since a single-value media column has no membership reading at all), with a driver-level repro in the dev's own table. Prime Directive #10: a reproducible defect takes a card. The dispatch seat should file it on ACCEPT (engine lane; the dev report's dedupe words apply) rather than leave it in acceptance notes. This PR neither depends on nor repeats the wrong prescription, so the verdict stands.

Check-runs on `3a0bcb2d`, read for this act at 2026-10-01T20:23Z: 34 runs: 25 success, 3 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke — path-filtered), 0 failed; STILL RUNNING at this write, so not reported as passed: `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (5/6)`, `Test Core (6/6)`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Lint & Repo Gates`. Every check must conclude green before the owning seat lands this (contract-review reference, pre-landing check ②); `Lint & Repo Gates` is the job that runs `check:migration-registry`, the gate on the regenerated `registry.ts` region, and this PASS does not stand in for its conclusion.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-21189-text-operator-entry-control`
Reviewed-by: `session_01UtnxvdiN376GF3sgXwAw4d`

**VERDICT: PASS**
